title: POC weekly sync - integration sanity & rate limits
next_steps: Redwood to run 10k token benchmark with customer's sample prompt set and share results (by 2026-04-27)
StratusHealth to provide representative failure logs and sample batched payloads (by 2026-04-24)
Schedule deep-dive on rate-limiting and spike protection with Priya and Samir (calendar invite)
action_items: Avery Patel: send sandbox credentials, sample SDK snippets, and security checklist (due: 2026-04-24)
Samir Khanna: run perf test with KV cache enabled + disabled and share CSV (due: 2026-04-27)
Daniel O'Connor: export recent 7 days of request/response traces and push to shared GCS (due: 2026-04-25)
Marta Ruiz: confirm pilot success criteria and max acceptable p50/p95 latencies (due: 2026-04-23)
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint focusing on SDK integration, function/tool calling behavior under load, structured output validation, and rate-limiting. Identified a few SDK edge cases around retries and streaming, agreed next steps for benchmarks and logs, and scheduled a technical deep dive on spike protection.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery Patel: Okay folks thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this to 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Marta Ruiz: Marta here.
[00:10] Daniel O'Connor: Daniel on platform.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Priya here.
[00:14] Elliot Wong: Elliot, product.
[00:16] Samir Khanna: Samir from Redwood.
[00:18] Jordan Lee: Jordan also from Redwood.
[00:20] Avery Patel: Great. Agenda — status on integration, any showstoppers, perf numbers update, and next steps.

[02:05] Marta Ruiz: Quick context, we've integrated the SDK into our staging app. Most flows working but the structured invoice extraction tool has been flaky, some fields missing or nested lists flattened wrong.

[02:40] Samir Khanna: When you say flattened, do you mean the JSON schema isn't matching? Could be the SDK's structured output parsing step, or the model is returning slightly different tokenization. Are you using the SDK's strict schema validation?

[03:05] Daniel O'Connor: We're using the Node SDK with the auto-parse flag turned on. Looks like when tool calling is triggered the SDK sometimes returns a plain string and not the function payload object. We suspect race on stream termination.

[03:40] Jordan Lee: That's consistent with a streaming boundary issue we saw in older SDK versions — there's a fix in 0.9.3 that improves function-call close events. Which version are you on?

[03:55] Marta Ruiz: 0.9.1 currently. We patched quickly to test, but haven't deployed the newer one.

[04:10] Avery Patel: Action item — we'll send the patched snippet and an annotated changelog for 0.9.3 after this call.

[05:00] Priya Nair: Separate note on rate limits: during our load tests Friday, we saw a sharp spike and our circuit breaker flipped. We need guidance on backpressure and recommended retry window.

[05:28] Samir Khanna: Two parts — client side and server side. For client side SDK we recommend exponential backoff with jitter and a max retry count of 3 for idempotent calls. For streaming/chat calls we suggest no automatic retry unless you can resume from a token offset or use prefix caching.

[06:10] Daniel O'Connor: The tricky part is our orchestrator batches 8 user messages into a single request. If that fails, it's costly to retry everything. Is there a way to split or partially retry?

[06:40] Jordan Lee: One pattern is to shard at the message-level and reconstitute on the server with a session id; another is to enable the prefix/KV cache so you only send deltas. Redwood's runtime supports KV cache per session so subsequent retries can be much smaller.

[07:20] Elliot Wong: Does KV cache maintain strict consistency? If we have multiple app servers routing to different inference pools, will cache misses cause divergence?

[07:40] Samir Khanna: Good q. The KV cache is sticky per session id but you can back it with a shared redis if you want strong consistency across nodes. For the hosted POC the cache is kept in the serving tier and is eventually consistent within a region.

[08:15] Marta Ruiz: Back to structured output — when function calling emits the tool payload, sometimes keys like 'amount_cents' become 'amount cents' or 'amt_cents' in the transcript. It's like tokenization is changing underscores.

[08:38] Samir Khanna: That sounds like a prompt tokenization artifact. Two mitigations — enforce explicit schema with the SDK (the parser will reject malformed keys) and add a post-processor normalizer in your mapping layer. We can show an example mapping; it's small.

[09:15] Daniel O'Connor: Can you show an example now?

[09:18] Samir Khanna: Sure. (screen share) So you define the expected function signature and the SDK will produce a JSON object with typed fields. If the model returns 'amount cents' instead of 'amount_cents' the parser will flag an error and surface the raw text so you can apply a deterministic normalization.

[10:05] Priya Nair: On observability, we need per-request token-level cost and latency. We saw an invoice where token cost spiked — want to find out which prompt variant triggered it.

[10:30] Jordan Lee: Console exposes per-route token breakdown and you can attach tracing headers from your app. If you send the trace ids, we can pull the full token logs. For the POC we can also share a limited retention export for debugging.

[11:00] Marta Ruiz: We'll share three suspect trace ids offline.

[11:20] Avery Patel: Moving to performance numbers — Samir, you ran the perf sweep last night?

[11:25] Samir Khanna: Yes. We did 1k concurrent small requests (avg 200 tokens) and a burst test with 200 concurrent large requests (avg 4k tokens). p50 was ~95ms for small requests on the dedicated pool, p95 ~230ms. For large requests p50 ~420ms, p95 ~1.1s. With KV cache enabled p50 for repeated patterns dropped by ~40%.

[12:05] Daniel O'Connor: That's promising. In our Friday run p95 was closer to 1.6s for large requests. What accounts for the difference?

[12:20] Samir Khanna: Likely batching and kernel selection — if your request mix has long sequences that prevent smaller requests from batching, effective throughput drops. Also check your quantization profile; we served with q4f32 on that sweep, which is faster but slightly lower quality than q8_0 in some cases.

[13:00] Elliot Wong: Can we get a recommended quant profile for our fidelity requirements? We're sensitive to hallucinations in invoice extraction.

[13:18] Jordan Lee: We recommend q8_0 or q8_1 for sensitive extraction tasks — slightly slower but higher fidelity. We'll include a short doc mapping profiles to tradeoffs.

[14:05] Marta Ruiz: We also hit an edge with function calling where embedded JSON inside a field caused parsing to stop. Eg: description: "{\"line_items\":[...]}" — nested JSON as string.

[14:30] Samir Khanna: Nested JSON in strings is tricky. Two options — ask the model to emit only top-level structured data (escape inner JSON as base64) or include a two-step call: first produce a normalized top-level structure, then a second tool to parse inner blobs. We'll demo both patterns.

[15:10] Priya Nair: Regarding retries and idempotency, what's Redwood's recommendation for non-idempotent function calls (e.g., creating invoices)?

[15:28] Samir Khanna: For non-idempotent operations, attach a client-generated idempotency key and persist the key on your side. If you must retry, do it only after verifying server state or using a two-phase commit pattern. The SDK can surface idempotency headers automatically.

[16:05] Daniel O'Connor: We have a separate DB write step after the LLM output; maybe we move to a compensated transaction flow. We'll evaluate.

[16:40] Jordan Lee: Quick note — there's a small bug in SDK 0.9.1 around streaming close events that causes the function-call wrapper to emit a trailing newline which some parsers treat as malformed JSON. 0.9.3 trims it.

[17:05] Marta Ruiz: Good to know. We'll plan to upgrade.

[17:40] Avery Patel: Any security/compliance questions?

[17:50] Priya Nair: Yes, two asks — where are logs stored, and do you support customer-managed KMS for embeddings?

[18:05] Samir Khanna: Logs for the POC are ephemeral and stored in region X; we can export audit logs to your GCS. For embeddings and private deployments we offer KMS integrations; for hosted we have a BYOK option via customer-managed KMS on the Private plan. We'll share the security whitepaper.

[19:00] Elliot Wong: Can we get a SOC2 scope summary? Our procurement needs that before pilot expansion.

[19:10] Avery Patel: Yes — I'll attach the SOC2 and encryption docs after the call.

[20:00] Marta Ruiz: One more operational thing — during spikes we saw 429s with no Retry-After header which made our orchestrator retry aggressively. Can Redwood add Retry-After and a per-route header for quota remaining?

[20:25] Samir Khanna: We can add Retry-After easily; quota-remaining header is in our roadmap and we can expose it for the POC via a flag. We'll assign an engineer to toggle it for your account.

[21:00] Daniel O'Connor: Appreciate that. It'd help throttling to be adaptive.

[21:30] Avery Patel: Quick recap of open items — SDK upgrade guidance, perf benchmark run with your prompt set, sample logs and traces, and a deep dive on rate-limiting. Any objections?

[22:00] Priya Nair: No objections. Also want to confirm the pilot success criteria — Marta?

[22:12] Marta Ruiz: We'll call it successful if p95 latency for invoice extraction under representative load is <1s and structured output schema passes 95% of our validation tests. Also cost per 1k tokens needs to stay within the budgetary guardrails Elliot will send.

[22:50] Elliot Wong: Will send budget numbers today.

[23:10] Jordan Lee: I'll follow up with a short integration checklist and a sample normalization function for keys.

[23:30] Samir Khanna: I'll run the KV/no-KV perf sweep and share CSVs plus the command lines we used.

[23:45] Avery Patel: All right, wrap up — we'll reconvene next week same time, and schedule the deep dive with Priya mid-week. Thanks everyone.

[24:05] Marta Ruiz: Thanks.
[24:08] Daniel O'Connor: Thanks all.
[24:10] Priya Nair: Bye.
[24:12] Elliot Wong: Bye.

[24:30] (call ends, recording stops)
